episode_title: The LNO Framework, High-Agency Product Management, and Avoiding Vanity Metrics
guest_title: Former Product Leader at Stripe, Twitter, Google, Yahoo
summary: Shreyas Doshi introduces the LNO Framework for PM time allocation (Leverage, Neutral, Overhead), how to avoid Goodhart's Law when selecting product metrics, and why pre-mortems prevent catastrophic launch failures.
transcript:
Lenny Rachitsky: Shreyas, you are legendary in the PM community for your frameworks. Let's start with the LNO Framework. Most PMs are drowning in unread Slack messages, Jira tickets, and meeting invites. How does LNO help product managers escape burnout?

Shreyas Doshi: Thanks Lenny. Most PMs make the fatal assumption that every task on their to-do list deserves their absolute best, 10/10 effort. That is the quickest path to burnout and mediocrity. Instead, classify every task into three buckets:

'L' is Leverage Tasks. These are 10x multiplier tasks: your product strategy, your annual PRD, your pricing model, coaching your star engineers. Doing an exceptional job here has disproportionate impact. You should give this 10/10 perfectionist effort.

'N' is Neutral Tasks. These are standard maintenance tasks: weekly status updates, sprint planning, customer bug triage. A good job (7/10) is completely fine. Nobody gets promoted for having the prettiest sprint backlog.

'O' is Overhead Tasks. These are administrative chores: expense reports, routine sign-offs, low-priority email. Your goal here is active satisficing: get them done fast, at 4/10 or 5/10 quality, in batch mode. If you spend your genius on overhead, you starve your leverage.

Lenny Rachitsky: You also caution heavily against Goodhart's Law in product metrics. How do growth teams corrupt their north star metric?

Shreyas Doshi: Goodhart's Law states: 'When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.' I see growth teams pick a single North Star metric, like daily active users or click-through rate, and gamify it with deceptive notifications or dark UX patterns. You see a temporary spike in DAU, but your 90-day churn explodes because you burned user trust.

Always pair your North Star metric with Counter-Metrics. If your goal is feature adoption, your counter-metric must be customer support tickets or uninstall rates. If your goal is signups, your counter-metric is 30-day retention. If you don't track the counter-metric, you will optimize your company right off a cliff.
